_README: Every test in kind auth's contract suite (tests/test-data-auth.js) that the ROW judge is
expected to disagree with, and why. Regenerate the NAMES with:
but never regenerate the REASONS mechanically — an entry without a reason someone wrote is
the whole thing this fixture exists to prevent.
Categories: default | field | create | harness | cosmetic | OPEN
SCOPE OF THIS CHECK: test-data-auth.js's fixtures declare NO authVocabulary, so every
run here exercises the LEGACY SHIM path (legacyVerbs.js). A migrated app does not use it —
all 81 pattern rows on rowauth-test declare, and a declared vocabulary wins over the shim.
The declared path is covered in tests/test-row-auth-writes.js, 'a DECLARED vocabulary'.
cascade: an edit that changes nothing passes with any of the row's edit permissions
U on a page: stranger 403, anon 401, editor 200
U judges the stored type, not the one the client names
_cascade_note: Not disagreements at all. test-data-auth.js's race test restores docsPage.authPermissions
AFTER its try/finally, so when its assertion fails it leaks users:{10:['edit-page']} into every
later test. These three then fail for that reason. Moving those two lines into the finally
takes the run from 26 failures to 23. Their file, their call — raised, not patched.

reasons.default: STRICT DEFAULTS, decided (hub). Kind auth: signed-in + no grants ⇒ open. Row auth: writes need a grant. Every app with unconfigured patterns loses editing on an enforce flip — the Phase D audit script is a prerequisite.
reasons.field: FIELD→VERB RULES, deliberately not implemented (owner, 2026-10-29): which attribute needs which verb is business logic and belongs in the pattern. Row auth is LOOSER here — publish-page, edit-page-params and edit-source-data stop being enforced server-side. May be revisited; it is an omission, not a gap.
reasons.create: WHAT A CREATE IS JUDGED AGAINST. Without a claimed parent_id the type path routes docs|page and docs|component to the same pattern row, so one `create` verb cannot tell 'add a section' from 'add a page'. Accepted: a page created with its sections IS 'add a page to this pattern'.
reasons.harness: NOT A DISAGREEMENT. These drive their race by hooking controller.getPatternRows — kind auth's pattern-grant lookup. The row judge never calls it, so the concurrent edit never fires. The protection they test (expect + assertRowUnchanged) is in the ROUTE, gate-independent and unchanged.
reasons.cosmetic: Behaviour is right (allowed under log, one line written). The assertion matches '[data-auth] … missing edit-page'; the row gate writes '[row-auth] … reason=missing edit'.
reasons.OPEN: SCOPE COLLAPSE — a real widening, nobody decided it. A FLAT grant of `edit-page` on a pattern row also confers editing the pattern ROW, because a flat grant expands against the union of self+descendants (expandWithVocabulary -> maps.flat), which is what flat has always meant. NOT a legacyVerbs problem: the declared vocabulary is ALREADY correctly scoped (edit-pattern under self, edit-page under descendants) and wins over the shim. The fix is in the GRANT, not the server: write it scoped, {descendants:{groups:{Editors:['edit-page']}}}, and the pattern row is untouched — verified in test-row-auth-writes.js. See planning/tasks/current/row-auth-scoped-grants.md. Measured exposure today: zero (no group grants on pattern rows in rowauth-test). Bound: ordinary fields only, never grants.
